content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore xpath namespaces within XPath. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: XPath Namespaces matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about namespace-qualified queries, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: XPath selects nodes and values from a data model. A location path is built from steps; predicates filter candidate nodes. Prefixes in a query must be bound by the host query context, even when the XML uses a different prefix for the same namespace URI.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: Namespace-qualified queries; Prefix registration in query contexts; Default namespaces and query behavior; Matching names across different prefixes. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: XPath Namespaces
content_blocks.expected_output: On a catalog containing products with numeric price child elements, this XPath selects the names of products whose price is greater than 10.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect this example as text. Run it only in a processor that supports the shown language/version; the standard CodeLeaf playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only and does not execute XML, XSD, XPath, XSLT, XQuery, Python, or SQL. Start with a small expression, compare it with the expected set of nodes, and then add one predicate at a time. XPath 1.0 and XPath 2.0/3.1 differ in data model and expression features, so record the processor and supported version.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the sample to its exact starting state before each experiment. Change one element, attribute, expression, or constraint at a time, then compare the result with the expected behavior.
content_blocks.limitations: XPath version support and namespace-prefix registration depend on the selected host application or query processor.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Record the exact processor and version: specification support is not universal, especially for XSD 1.1, XPath 2.0/3.1, XQuery, and XSLT 2.0/3.0.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small synthetic example that demonstrates “Namespace-qualified queries”. Then add one boundary case involving “Prefix registration in query contexts”. Write down what should happen before testing, and record the exact output or processor message afterward.
